newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen HU shows telecommunications losses.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen HU shows telecommunications losses.

text.p: Thyssen Handelsunion AG, trade and services arm of the Thyssen Group, said on Thursday it had posted a loss of 178.3 million marks on its share of E-Plus Mobilfunk GmbH.
Handelsunion chairman Hans-Erich Forster said the loss was within plan, given the start-up nature of the business, which entails outlays for capital infrastructure.

Subsidiary Thyssen Telecom AG also showed a loss of 66 million marks. Thyssen Handelsunion invested 357.1 million marks in Thyssen Telecom in the year ended September 30, over one-third of its total group investment of 941.4 million marks.
Comparison figures were not immediately available.
E-Plus, with 500,000 customers, is a distant third in Germany's mobile phone market. The mobile units of Deutsche Telekom AG and Mannesmann AG each have more than 2.2 million customers.
Thyssen Telecom, which had been a leading contender for an alliance with DBKom, the telecommunications arm of national railway Deutsche Bahn AG, last year lost that bid to its competitor Mannesmann.
Thyssen and German utility Veba AG each hold 30 ppercent stakes in E-Plus. BellSouth Corp. of the United States and Britain's Vodafone Group Plc each have 20 percent shares.

Since the DBKom debacle, Thyssen would concentrate its telecommunications activities on those areas of the business it can handle alone, without an alliance with a strong, permanent partner, Forster said.
"Naturally we do not exclude cooperation in certain project phases. But overall we deem it sensible not to make our own success dependent on the well-being of a partnership," Forster said.
Thyssen's telecommunications strategy will rest on its mobile phone units E-Plus and DFR, its fixed network PlusNet, and multimedia services for other network operators, he said.
